status: experimental interoperability profile; no production promotion claimed
scope: Composition of stable root identity, service-scoped relationship/delegation evidence, first-hop endpoint-currentness evidence, accountable operator or organization credentials, and local authorization. The profile is protocol-neutral and does not require DID resolution, AID, PKA, DNSSEC, DANE, OAuth, MCP, A2A, or any single identity system.
core_invariant: Stable identity continuity, service relationship/delegation, endpoint currency, accountability, and authorization are separate evidence/decision planes. Success in any identity or discovery plane MUST NOT create local effect authority.

planes.answers: Which key/endpoint is currently evidenced for this service relationship?
What longer-lived root and service relationship is evidenced across service-key rotation?
What operator or organization credential stands behind the identity?
What exact action may this principal perform here and now?

composition_pattern: stable root identity -> signed attenuation-only service relationship/delegation -> service-specific identity/key -> platform-local identity or endpoint-currentness proof -> authentication -> local policy evaluation -> bounded grant -> effect
required_properties: root keys are not required for ordinary service traffic
service-specific keys isolate compromise and rotation blast radius
service compromise does not imply unrelated service or root compromise absent separate evidence
root compromise invalidates unrevalidated descendant service relationships even if endpoint keys remain current
endpoint-key replacement does not silently replace persistent identity
endpoint-key replacement does not automatically transfer grants bound to the retired key
platform-specific service credentials are audience/service bound and cannot be replayed as cross-platform authority
pairwise or service-specific presentation identifiers need not expose cross-service correlation without separate authorized linkage evidence
lineage evidence never mints scopes, capabilities, grants, or permissions
delegation cannot widen authority beyond its parent and cannot substitute for a local grant
stale endpoint or lineage evidence fails closed at a consequential effect boundary
protocol transitions cannot widen action, purpose, destination, audience, resource, budget, or expiry
root compromise is a distinct recovery class from service-key compromise
pre-compromise lineage requires explicit revalidation or a separate local recovery policy after root compromise
nonclaims: This profile does not make a DID an endpoint-discovery primitive.
This profile does not require a generic identity document in first-hop discovery.
This profile does not claim DNS or any identity proof is globally current.
This profile does not require pairwise identifiers in every deployment.
This profile does not grant legal identity, personhood, reputation, truth, execution authority, or delegation authority.
